claim: Huntington's disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder with no curative or preventative treatment options.
source: Huntington's disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder with no curative or preventative treatment options.
evidence: This is a statement of established medical knowledge about HD.

claim: HD is caused by the expansion of a translated CAG trinucleotide repeat within exon 1 of the huntingtin gene (HTT).
source: The disease is caused by the expansion of a translated CAG trinucleotide repeat within exon 1 of the huntingtin gene (HTT), resulting in a mutant huntingtin (mHtt) protein with an abnormally long N-terminal tract of glutamine residues (Ross and Tabrizi, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ross and Tabrizi, 2011.

claim: The CAG repeat expansion results in a mutant huntingtin (mHtt) protein with an abnormally long N-terminal tract of glutamine residues.
source: The disease is caused by the expansion of a translated CAG trinucleotide repeat within exon 1 of the huntingtin gene (HTT), resulting in a mutant huntingtin (mHtt) protein with an abnormally long N-terminal tract of glutamine residues (Ross and Tabrizi, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ross and Tabrizi, 2011.

claim: Individuals with more than 36 to 39 CAG repeats develop HD.
source: Individuals with more than 36 to 39 repeats develop the disorder, and the length of the repeat correlates with the age of disease onset (Walker, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Walker, 2007.

claim: The length of the CAG repeat correlates with the age of disease onset.
source: Individuals with more than 36 to 39 repeats develop the disorder, and the length of the repeat correlates with the age of disease onset (Walker, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Walker, 2007.

claim: The poly-glutamine repeat expansion impacts the physical properties of the huntingtin protein.
source: The poly-glutamine repeat expansion impacts the physical (Kazantsev et al., 1999) and physiological (Hipp et al., 2012; Verhoef et al., 2002; Fernandez-Estevez et al., 2014) properties of the huntingtin protein, producing aggregates in aged striatal neurons that eventually precipitate to form neuronal inclusion bodies (Miller et al., 2010a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kazantsev et al., 1999.

claim: The poly-glutamine repeat expansion impacts the physiological properties of the huntingtin protein.
source: The poly-glutamine repeat expansion impacts the physical (Kazantsev et al., 1999) and physiological (Hipp et al., 2012; Verhoef et al., 2002; Fernandez-Estevez et al., 2014) properties of the huntingtin protein, producing aggregates in aged striatal neurons that eventually precipitate to form neuronal inclusion bodies (Miller et al., 2010a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hipp et al., 2012; Verhoef et al., 2002; Fernandez-Estevez et al., 2014.

claim: The poly-glutamine repeat expansion produces aggregates in aged striatal neurons that eventually precipitate to form neuronal inclusion bodies.
source: The poly-glutamine repeat expansion impacts the physical (Kazantsev et al., 1999) and physiological (Hipp et al., 2012; Verhoef et al., 2002; Fernandez-Estevez et al., 2014) properties of the huntingtin protein, producing aggregates in aged striatal neurons that eventually precipitate to form neuronal inclusion bodies (Miller et al., 2010a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Miller et al., 2010a.

claim: Accumulation of mHtt triggers a variety of insults that lead to striatal degeneration.
source: Accumulation of mHtt triggers a variety of insults that lead to striatal degeneration, however, the nature of the specific mHtt species, soluble, oligomeric or aggregate, that triggers neurodegeneration remains unclear (Arrasate et al., 2004; Lajoie and Snapp, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Arrasate et al., 2004; Lajoie and Snapp, 2010.

claim: The nature of the specific mHtt species (soluble, oligomeric or aggregate) that triggers neurodegeneration remains unclear.
source: Accumulation of mHtt triggers a variety of insults that lead to striatal degeneration, however, the nature of the specific mHtt species, soluble, oligomeric or aggregate, that triggers neurodegeneration remains unclear (Arrasate et al., 2004; Lajoie and Snapp, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Arrasate et al., 2004; Lajoie and Snapp, 2010.

claim: PIP4Kγ is a lipid kinase expressed by the PIP4K2C gene.
source: PIP4Kγ [Phosphatidylinositol-5-phosphate 4-kinase, type II γ] is a lipid kinase expressed by the PIP4K2C gene.
evidence: This is a statement of established biochemical knowledge.

claim: PIP4Kγ is predominantly localized in several tissues, including the brain.
source: The protein is predominantly localized in several tissues, including the brain (Sasaki et al., 2009; Rameh et al., 1997; Clarke et al., 2008; Clarke et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Sasaki et al., 2009; Rameh et al., 1997; Clarke et al., 2008; Clarke et al., 2009.

claim: PIP4Kγ phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol-5-phosphate [PI5P] to produce phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2].
source: Enzymatically, PIP4Kγ phosphorylates phosphatidylinositol-5-phosphate [PI5P] to produce phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate [PI(4,5)P2] (Lietha, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lietha, 2011.

claim: The biological function of PIP4Kγ is not completely understood.
source: The biological function of PIP4Kγ is not completely understood, although recent reports suggest a role in the modulation of vesicle trafficking (Clarke et al., 2008), and mTOR signaling (Mackey et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: Recent reports suggest PIP4Kγ has a role in the modulation of vesicle trafficking.
source: The biological function of PIP4Kγ is not completely understood, although recent reports suggest a role in the modulation of vesicle trafficking (Clarke et al., 2008), and mTOR signaling (Mackey et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Clarke et al., 2008.

claim: Recent reports suggest PIP4Kγ has a role in mTOR signaling.
source: The biological function of PIP4Kγ is not completely understood, although recent reports suggest a role in the modulation of vesicle trafficking (Clarke et al., 2008), and mTOR signaling (Mackey et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Mackey et al., 2014.

claim: NCT-504 is an analogue obtained upon medicinal chemistry optimization of a series of 5-phenylthieno[2,3-d]pyrimidine compounds identified in a high-throughput phenotypic screen.
source: NCT-504 (Figure 1A) is an analogue obtained upon medicinal chemistry optimization of a series of 5-phenylthieno[2,3-d]pyrimidine compounds identified in a high-throughput phenotypic screen (Titus, 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Titus, 2010.

claim: Expression of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q103 in PC12 cells produces detergent-resistant GFP-labeled aggregates.
source: Expression of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q103 in PC12 cells produces detergent-resistant GFP-labeled aggregates (Titus et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Titus et al., 2012.

claim: NCT-504 caused a robust reduction of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q103 levels in PC12 cells, as measured by lowered GFP signal.
source: NCT-504 caused a robust reduction of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q103 levels, as measured by lowered GFP signal (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: NCT-504 treatment decreased huntingtin aggregates in HEK293T cells transiently transfected with GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q74.
source: NCT-504 treatment also decreased huntingtin aggregates in HEK293T cells transiently transfected with GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q74 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: NCT-504 was active against only a single kinase, PIP4Kγ, in a panel of 442 human kinases using a cutoff of >65% inhibition at 10 μM.
source: Using a cutoff of >65% inhibition at 10 μM, NCT-504 was active against only a single kinase, PIP4Kγ (Table 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Table 1.

claim: ML168 had activity against six kinases in a panel of 442 human kinases, but was most potent against PIP4Kγ.
source: Similarly, another analogue from the same thienopyrimidine series, ML168 (Titus, 2010), had activity against six kinases in the same panel, but was most potent against PIP4Kγ.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Titus, 2010 and implies data from the kinase panel.

claim: NCT-504 modulated the activity of PIP4Kγ in the DiscoverX binding assay with a Kd = 354 nM.
source: NCT-504 modulated the activity of PIP4Kγ in the DiscoverX binding assay (https://www.discoverx.com/services/drug-discovery-development-services/kinase-profiling/kinomescan) with a Kd = 354 nM (Figure 1D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: NCT-504 inhibited PIP4Kγ enzyme activity with an IC50 of 15.8 μM in a reconstituted assay of phosphorylation of the PI5P substrate by full length PIP4Kγ.
source: Using a reconstituted assay of phosphorylation of the PI5P substrate by full length PIP4Kγ, NCT-504 inhibited enzyme activity with an IC50 of 15.8 μM (Figure 1E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In the absence of PI5P substrate, NCT-504 did not impair the intrinsic ATP-hydrolytic activity of PIP4Kγ.
source: Notably, in the absence of PI5P substrate, the compound did not impair the intrinsic ATP-hydrolytic activity of PIP4Kγ (Figure 1F), suggesting that NCT-504 is an allosteric inhibitor of this kinase.
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: NCT-504 is an allosteric inhibitor of PIP4Kγ.
source: Notably, in the absence of PI5P substrate, the compound did not impair the intrinsic ATP-hydrolytic activity of PIP4Kγ (Figure 1F), suggesting that NCT-504 is an allosteric inhibitor of this kinase.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the data in Figure 1F showing no impairment of ATP-hydrolytic activity in the absence of substrate.

claim: 50 μM NCT-504 did not inhibit PIP4Kbeta or PIP4Kalpha (IC50 between 50 μM and 100 μM) in isolated enzyme assays.
source: In isolated enzyme assays against other PIP4K isoforms, 50 μM NCT-504 did not inhibit PIP4Kbeta or PIP4Kalpha (IC50 between 50 μM and 100 μM) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: NCT-504 was largely inactive against PIP4Kγ+ with a potency >500 μM.
source: NCT-504 was largely inactive against PIP4Kγ+ with a potency >500 μM (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Exposure to NCT-504 elevated cellular levels of PI5P in wild type mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: As expected, exposure to NCT-504 elevated cellular levels of PI5P (Figure 2D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: NCT-504 robustly increased PI(3,5)P2 levels in wild type mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: Surprisingly, NCT-504 also robustly increased PI(3,5)P2 levels, and to a lesser extent increased levels of PI3P (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2B and E.

claim: NCT-504 increased levels of PI3P to a lesser extent than PI(3,5)P2 in wild type mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: Surprisingly, NCT-504 also robustly increased PI(3,5)P2 levels, and to a lesser extent increased levels of PI3P (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2B and E.

claim: NCT-504 did not have an effect on PI(4,5)P2 levels in wild type mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: We did not observe an effect on PI(4,5)P2 levels (Figure 2F), which is consistent with other reports indicating that the cellular levels of this lipid are mostly generated from PI4P via type I PI4P 5-kinases (Lietha, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2F and a citation to Lietha, 2011.

claim: The cellular levels of PI(4,5)P2 are mostly generated from PI4P via type I PI4P 5-kinases.
source: We did not observe an effect on PI(4,5)P2 levels (Figure 2F), which is consistent with other reports indicating that the cellular levels of this lipid are mostly generated from PI4P via type I PI4P 5-kinases (Lietha, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Lietha, 2011.

claim: NCT-504 causes an increase in PI5P, PI(3,5)P2 and PI3P levels along with a decrease in PI4P, progressively over 12 hr.
source: Kinetic measurement of PI levels showed that NCT-504 causes an increase in PI5P, PI(3,5)P2 and PI3P levels along with a decrease in PI4P, progressively over 12 hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The statistically significant changes in PI levels caused by NCT-504 were not observed at 30 or 120 min.
source: These statistically significant changes were not observed at 30 or 120 min suggesting that direct inhibition of PIP4Kγ eventually impacts other lipid kinases and phosphatases.
evidence: This statement is based on data from kinetic measurements.

claim: Direct inhibition of PIP4Kγ eventually impacts other lipid kinases and phosphatases.
source: These statistically significant changes were not observed at 30 or 120 min suggesting that direct inhibition of PIP4Kγ eventually impacts other lipid kinases and phosphatases.
evidence: This is inferred from the delayed changes in PI levels.

claim: Treatment of unaffected human fibroblasts with NCT-504 elevated PI5P, PI(3,5)P2, and PI3P in a dose dependent manner.
source: Moreover treatment of unaffected human fibroblasts with NCT-504 elevated these three lipids in a dose dependent manner (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: shRNA-mediated silencing of PIP4Kγ resulted in an elevation of PI5P, PI(3,5)P2 and PI3P.
source: Further evidence that the changes in PI levels are due to the specific inhibition of PIP4Kγ, is the finding that shRNA-mediated silencing of PIP4Kγ resulted in a similar PI profile to that observed with NCT-504 inhibition, namely an elevation of PI5P, PI(3,5)P2 and PI3P (Figure 2B,D and E).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2B, D and E.

claim: During shRNA-mediated silencing of PIP4Kγ transcripts, PIP4Kγ protein was no longer detected.
source: Note that during shRNA-mediated silencing of PIP4Kγ transcripts, PIP4Kγ protein was no longer detected (Figure 2G).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: mHtt upregulates autophagy, but impairs incorporation of client proteins into autophagosomes.
source: Numerous studies have shown that mHtt upregulates autophagy, but impairs incorporation of client proteins into autophagosomes (Cortes and La Spada, 2014; Ochaba et al., 2014; Martin et al., 2015; Martinez-Vicente et al., 2010; Tsvetkov et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Cortes and La Spada, 2014; Ochaba et al., 2014; Martin et al., 2015; Martinez-Vicente et al., 2010; Tsvetkov et al., 2013.

claim: A number of autophagy modulators have been described that reduce mHtt aggregates.
source: Importantly, a number of autophagy modulators have been described that reduce mHtt aggregates (Sarkar et al., 2009; Roscic et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2007; Renna et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Sarkar et al., 2009; Roscic et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2007; Renna et al., 2010.

claim: A two hour incubation of HEK293T cells with 5 or 10 μM NCT-504 did not significantly increase LC3-II levels.
source: We tested and found that a two hour incubation of HEK293T cells with 5 or 10 μM NCT-504 did not significantly increase LC3-II levels (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Treating HEK293T cells with 10 μM NCT-504 and 100 nM bafilomycin A1 for two hours resulted in a 38% increase in LC3-II levels compared with bafilomycin A1 treatment alone.
source: Importantly, treating cells with 10 μM NCT-504 and 100 nM bafilomycin A1 for two hours and six hours resulted in a 38% and 51% increase in LC3-II levels respectively compared with bafilomycin A1 treatment alone, which indicates that NCT-504 induces autophagosome formation.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from LC3-II measurements.

claim: Treating HEK293T cells with 10 μM NCT-504 and 100 nM bafilomycin A1 for six hours resulted in a 51% increase in LC3-II levels compared with bafilomycin A1 treatment alone.
source: Importantly, treating cells with 10 μM NCT-504 and 100 nM bafilomycin A1 for two hours and six hours resulted in a 38% and 51% increase in LC3-II levels respectively compared with bafilomycin A1 treatment alone, which indicates that NCT-504 induces autophagosome formation.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from LC3-II measurements.

claim: NCT-504 induces autophagosome formation.
source: Importantly, treating cells with 10 μM NCT-504 and 100 nM bafilomycin A1 for two hours and six hours resulted in a 38% and 51% increase in LC3-II levels respectively compared with bafilomycin A1 treatment alone, which indicates that NCT-504 induces autophagosome formation.
evidence: This is inferred from the increase in LC3-II levels in the presence of bafilomycin A1.

claim: Treating HEK293T cells with 5 μM NCT-504 and bafilomycin A1 for two hours resulted in a 30% increase in LC3-II levels.
source: Similarly, treating cells with 5 μM NCT-504 and bafilomycin A1 for two and six hours resulted in a 30% and 46% increase in LC3-II levels respectively.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from LC3-II measurements.

claim: Treating HEK293T cells with 5 μM NCT-504 and bafilomycin A1 for six hours resulted in a 46% increase in LC3-II levels.
source: Similarly, treating cells with 5 μM NCT-504 and bafilomycin A1 for two and six hours resulted in a 30% and 46% increase in LC3-II levels respectively.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from LC3-II measurements.

claim: An elevation in LC3-II levels by NCT-504 in the presence of bafilomycin A1 but not in the absence of bafilomycin A1 suggests that NCT-504 elevates both the induction of autophagy as well as the rate of turnover of autophagic cargo (autophagy flux).
source: Importantly, an elevation in LC3-II levels by NCT-504 in the presence of bafilomycin A1 but not in the absence of bafilomycin A1, suggests that NCT-504 elevates both the induction of autophagy as well as the rate of turnover of autophagic cargo (autophagy flux).
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of NCT-504 with and without bafilomycin A1.

claim: NCT-504 treatment caused a robust increase in the formation of autolysosomes with only a modest elevation in autophagosomes.
source: In contrast, NCT-504 treatment caused a robust increase in the formation of autolysosomes with only a modest elevation in autophagosomes, which indicates that NCT-504 increases autophagic flux, with only a modest increase in autophagy initiation.
evidence: This statement is based on data from GFP-mCherry-LC3 reporter experiments.

claim: NCT-504 increases autophagic flux, with only a modest increase in autophagy initiation.
source: In contrast, NCT-504 treatment caused a robust increase in the formation of autolysosomes with only a modest elevation in autophagosomes, which indicates that NCT-504 increases autophagic flux, with only a modest increase in autophagy initiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects on autolysosomes versus autophagosomes.

claim: Treatment of rat primary cortical neurons expressing Dendra2-LC3 with either 500 nM or 1 µM NCT-504 enhanced the rate of Dendra2-LC3 turnover.
source: Importantly, treatment of rat primary cortical neurons expressing Dendra2-LC3 with either 500 nM or 1 µM NCT-504 enhanced the rate of Dendra2-LC3 turnover.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from Dendra2-LC3 photoconversion experiments.

claim: NCT-504 stimulates autophagy flux in primary rodent cortical neurons in a statistically significant manner up to 72 hr following treatment.
source: Thus, NCT-504 stimulates autophagy flux in primary rodent cortical neurons in a statistically significant manner up to 72 hr following treatment.
evidence: This statement is based on data from Dendra2-LC3 turnover experiments.

claim: NCT 504 treatment resulted in a dose dependent decrease of Htt protein levels in 293A cells at levels that did not impact cell viability.
source: Using this assay, we found that NCT 504 treatment resulted in a dose dependent decrease of Htt protein levels at levels that did not impact cell viability (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: NCT-504 lowered the levels of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q74 aggregates in Atg7+/+ MEF.
source: We found that while NCT-504 lowered the levels of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q74 aggregates in Atg7+/+ MEF, it failed to lower aggregates in Atg7-/- MEF; Atg7 is essential for autophagosome formation and its loss inhibits the autophagy pathway (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: NCT-504 failed to lower GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q74 aggregates in Atg7-/- MEF.
source: We found that while NCT-504 lowered the levels of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q74 aggregates in Atg7+/+ MEF, it failed to lower aggregates in Atg7-/- MEF; Atg7 is essential for autophagosome formation and its loss inhibits the autophagy pathway (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Atg7 is essential for autophagosome formation and its loss inhibits the autophagy pathway.
source: We found that while NCT-504 lowered the levels of GFP-Htt(exon1)-Q74 aggregates in Atg7+/+ MEF, it failed to lower aggregates in Atg7-/- MEF; Atg7 is essential for autophagosome formation and its loss inhibits the autophagy pathway (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Atg7.

claim: Treatment with 5 μM NCT-504 for 12 hr significantly reduced mHtt levels in fibroblasts from HD patient HD(Q68).
source: Notably, treatment with 5 μM NCT-504 for 12 hr, conditions that did not affect cell viability (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), significantly reduced mHtt levels in fibroblasts from two different HD patients HD(Q68) or HD(Q45) (Figure 4A and C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Treatment with 5 μM NCT-504 for 12 hr significantly reduced mHtt levels in fibroblasts from HD patient HD(Q45).
source: Notably, treatment with 5 μM NCT-504 for 12 hr, conditions that did not affect cell viability (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), significantly reduced mHtt levels in fibroblasts from two different HD patients HD(Q68) or HD(Q45) (Figure 4A and C).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Only silencing of PIP4K2C exhibited an appreciable and robust reduction of huntingtin protein levels in HD(Q68) patient fibroblast cell line.
source: To further test whether the reduction of mHtt levels was due to selective modulation of PIP4Kγ, we individually silenced PIP4K2A, PIP4K2B and PIP4K2C RNA in the HD(Q68) patient fibroblast cell line. Only silencing of PIP4K2C exhibited an appreciable and robust reduction of huntingtin protein levels (Figure 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Treatment of STHdhQ111 striatal cell line with 5 μM NCT-504 for 12 hr resulted in a 40% decrease in mHtt levels.
source: We treated a striatal cell line from a knock-in HD mouse (STHdhQ111) (Trettel et al., 2000), with 5 μM NCT-504 for 12 hr and observed a 40% decrease in mHtt levels (Figure 4D).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4D and a citation to Trettel et al., 2000.

claim: Concentrations of NCT-504 of 5 μM or lower did not impact the viability of cortical neurons.
source: We tested and found that concentrations of NCT-504 of 5 μM or lower did not impact the viability of cortical neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: 2.5 or 5 μM NCT-504 lowered the levels of Htt(exon1)-Q74 in primary cortical neurons.
source: Importantly, 2.5 or 5 μM NCT-504 lowered the levels of Htt(exon1)-Q74 in primary cortical neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A.

claim: Depletion of PIP4Kγ in cortical neurons via PIP4K2C-shRNA treatment led to a decrease in Htt(exon1)-Q74 levels and Htt(exon1)-Q74 aggregates.
source: Moreover, depletion of PIP4Kγ in cortical neurons via PIP4K2C-shRNA treatment also led to a decrease in Htt(exon1)-Q74 levels and Htt(exon1)-Q74 aggregates (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: NCT-504 treatment and PIP4K2C silencing each reduced Htt(exon1)-polyQ aggregates in neuroblastoma N2a cells transfected with Htt(exon1)-polyQ mutants.
source: Furthermore, NCT-504 treatment and PIP4K2C silencing each reduced Htt(exon1)-polyQ aggregates in neuroblastoma N2a cells transfected with Htt(exon1)-polyQ mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Reducing dPIP4K activity with either one of two different shRNAs ameliorated mHtt-induced photoreceptor degeneration in Drosophila.
source: Control HD model animals with wild-type activity of dPIP4K show prominent mHtt-induced photoreceptor degeneration. This phenotype is ameliorated by reducing dPIP4K activity with either one of two different shRNAs (Figure 5A).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Reducing the activity of dPIP4K using a loss-of-function mutant allele in heterozygosis ameliorated mHtt-induced motor impairment in Drosophila.
source: Neuronal-specific expression of HttN231Q128 leads to a late-onset motor impairment that can be quantified in a climbing assay. This phenotype was also ameliorated by reducing the activity of dPIP4K using a previously described (Gupta et al., 2013) classical loss-of-function mutant allele in heterozygosis and a kinase dead allele (Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5B and a citation to Gupta et al., 2013.

claim: Reducing the activity of dPIP4K using a kinase dead allele ameliorated mHtt-induced motor impairment in Drosophila.
source: Neuronal-specific expression of HttN231Q128 leads to a late-onset motor impairment that can be quantified in a climbing assay. This phenotype was also ameliorated by reducing the activity of dPIP4K using a previously described (Gupta et al., 2013) classical loss-of-function mutant allele in heterozygosis and a kinase dead allele (Figure 5B).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5B and a citation to Gupta et al., 2013.

claim: Decreasing the levels of PIP4K mitigated the motor performance decline in a full-length HD Drosophila model expressing Htt with a 200 polyQ expansion.
source: Additionally, we also evaluated these approaches (loss-of-function by a heterozygous mutant allele and kinase dead allele) in animals expressing full length Htt carrying a 200 polyQ expansion in exon1. Notably, we observed a mitigation of the motor performance decline in this full-length HD model.
evidence: This statement is based on data from motor performance assays in Drosophila.

claim: Decreasing the levels of PIP4K in the absence of mHtt did not affect motor performance when compared to controls in Drosophila.
source: Decreasing the levels of PIP4K with the same alleles in the absence of mHtt did not affect motor performance when compared to controls (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition or knock-down of PIP4Kγ modulates the equilibrium between phosphatidylinositide (PI) species within the cell and increases basal autophagy.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or knock-down of PIP4Kγ modulates the equilibrium between phosphatidylinositide (PI) species within the cell and increases basal autophagy, reducing the total amount of mHtt protein in human patient fibroblasts and aggregates in neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by data on PI levels and autophagy measurements.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition or knock-down of PIP4Kγ reduces the total amount of mHtt protein in human patient fibroblasts.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or knock-down of PIP4Kγ modulates the equilibrium between phosphatidylinositide (PI) species within the cell and increases basal autophagy, reducing the total amount of mHtt protein in human patient fibroblasts and aggregates in neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from patient fibroblast experiments.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition or knock-down of PIP4Kγ reduces mHtt aggregates in neurons.
source: Pharmacological inhibition or knock-down of PIP4Kγ modulates the equilibrium between phosphatidylinositide (PI) species within the cell and increases basal autophagy, reducing the total amount of mHtt protein in human patient fibroblasts and aggregates in neurons.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from neuronal experiments.

claim: Genetic knockdown of PIP4K ameliorated neuronal dysfunction and degeneration in two Drosophila models of Huntington's disease.
source: In two Drosophila models of Huntington's disease, genetic knockdown of PIP4K ameliorated neuronal dysfunction and degeneration as assessed using motor performance and retinal degeneration assays respectively.
evidence: This statement is supported by data from Drosophila experiments.

claim: PIP4Kγ is a druggable target whose inhibition enhances productive autophagy and mHtt proteolysis.
source: Together, these results suggest that PIP4Kγ is a druggable target whose inhibition enhances productive autophagy and mHtt proteolysis, revealing a useful pharmacological point of intervention for the treatment of Huntington's disease, and potentially for other neurodegenerative disorders.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Inhibition of PIP4Kγ reveals a useful pharmacological point of intervention for the treatment of Huntington's disease.
source: Together, these results suggest that PIP4Kγ is a druggable target whose inhibition enhances productive autophagy and mHtt proteolysis, revealing a useful pharmacological point of intervention for the treatment of Huntington's disease, and potentially for other neurodegenerative disorders.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the collective data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Inhibition of PIP4Kγ may be a useful pharmacological point of intervention for other neurodegenerative disorders.
source: Together, these results suggest that PIP4Kγ is a druggable target whose inhibition enhances productive autophagy and mHtt proteolysis, revealing a useful pharmacological point of intervention for the treatment of Huntington's disease, and potentially for other neurodegenerative disorders.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications beyond HD.

claim: NCT-504 is exquisitely selective in the kinase profiling assay, which may be explained by its function as an allosteric inhibitor.
source: NCT-504 function as an allosteric inhibitor may also explain why NCT-504 is exquisitely selective in the kinase profiling assay.
evidence: This is inferred from the selectivity data and the allosteric mechanism.

claim: Differences in potency between the enzymatic assay and the DiscoverX binding assay have been observed for allosteric modulators of other kinases.
source: Similar differences in potency between these two assays have also been observed for allosteric modulators of other kinases (Rudolf et al., 2014; Smyth and Collins, 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Rudolf et al., 2014; Smyth and Collins, 2009.

claim: Long-term inhibition of PIP4Kγ indirectly results in the activation of PIKfyve.
source: This raises the possibility that long-term inhibition of PIP4Kγ indirectly results in the activation of PIKfyve.
evidence: This is inferred from the elevation of PI(3,5)P2 and PI5P after 12 hr of NCT-504 treatment.

claim: Activation of PIKfyve may account for the increase in PI5P as well as PI(3,5)P2 following NCT-504 treatment.
source: This activation of PIKfyve may account for the increase in PI5P as well as PI(3,5)P2 (Zolov et al., 2012; McCartney et al., 2014; Sbrissa et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Zolov et al., 2012; McCartney et al., 2014; Sbrissa et al., 2012.

claim: At 12 hr, PI3P levels increased 1.3 fold following NCT-504 treatment, suggesting that VPS34 may be indirectly activated.
source: In addition, at 12 hr PI3P levels increased 1.3 fold, suggesting that VPS34 may be indirectly activated as well.
evidence: This is inferred from the increase in PI3P levels.

claim: The elevation of PI3P, PI(3,5)P2 and/or PI5P likely contribute to the elevation in autophagic flux.
source: The elevation of PI3P, PI(3,5)P2 and/or PI5P likely contribute to the elevation in autophagic flux.
evidence: This is inferred from the known roles of these lipids in autophagy.

claim: PI3P has well characterized roles in autophagy, acting in initiation of phagophore formation as well as in later steps of autophagosome maturation.
source: PI3P has well characterized roles in autophagy, and acts in initiation of phagophore formation (Shibutani and Yoshimori, 2014) as well as in later steps of autophagosome maturation (Carlsson and Simonsen, 2015), including autophagosome-lysosome fusion (Ikonomov et al., 2006) and lysosome reformation (Rong et al., 2012; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Shibutani and Yoshimori, 2014; Carlsson and Simonsen, 2015; Ikonomov et al., 2006; Rong et al., 2012; Yu et al., 2010.

claim: In some conditions, PI5P can induce autophagy independent of PI3P.
source: In some conditions, PI5P can induce autophagy independent of PI3P (Vicinanza et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Vicinanza et al., 2015.

claim: PI(3,5)P2 functions at a late step in autophagy.
source: In contrast, PI(3,5)P2 functions at a late step in autophagy (Ikonomov et al., 2006; de Lartigue et al., 2009; Jin et al., 2008; Jin et al., 2014; Ikonomov et al., 2001; Martin et al., 2013; Rusten et al., 2007; Sano et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Ikonomov et al., 2006; de Lartigue et al., 2009; Jin et al., 2008; Jin et al., 2014; Ikonomov et al., 2001; Martin et al., 2013; Rusten et al., 2007; Sano et al., 2016.

claim: A reduction of PI4P has been postulated to be necessary for lysosome reformation.
source: A reduction of PI4P has been postulated to be necessary for lysosome reformation (Rong et al., 2012; Yu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Rong et al., 2012; Yu et al., 2010.

claim: Several studies have indicated that there are polyglutamine-dependent alterations in PI binding of huntingtin protein.
source: Several studies have indicated that there are polyglutamine-dependent alterations in PI binding of huntingtin protein (Burke et al., 2013; Kegel et al., 2009a; Kegel et al., 2009b; Kegel et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Burke et al., 2013; Kegel et al., 2009a; Kegel et al., 2009b; Kegel et al., 2005.

claim: Wild-type huntingtin binds phosphoinositide lipids including PI5P and PI(3,5)P2.
source: Moreover, wild-type huntingtin binds phosphoinositide lipids including PI5P and PI(3,5)P2 (Kegel et al., 2009b).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kegel et al., 2009b.

claim: When assessed using unilamellar vesicles, huntingtin with a polyglutamine expansion bound PI5P and PI(3,5)P2 even more tightly than wild-type huntingtin.
source: Notably, when assessed using unilamellar vesicles, huntingtin with a polyglutamine expansion bound these lipids even more tightly than wild-type hungtingtin, potentially reducing the free total levels of these lipids and impacting their downstream dependent signaling (Kegel-Gleason, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kegel-Gleason, 2013.

claim: Huntingtin with a polyglutamine expansion binding PI5P and PI(3,5)P2 more tightly than wild-type huntingtin potentially reduces the free total levels of these lipids and impacts their downstream dependent signaling.
source: Notably, when assessed using unilamellar vesicles, huntingtin with a polyglutamine expansion bound these lipids even more tightly than wild-type hungtingtin, potentially reducing the free total levels of these lipids and impacting their downstream dependent signaling (Kegel-Gleason, 2013).
evidence: This is inferred from the tighter binding of mutant huntingtin to these lipids.

claim: Masking of PI lipids could negatively and progressively impact the function of proteins involved in autophagosome cargo recognition and loading.
source: Masking of PI lipids could negatively and progressively impact the function of proteins involved in autophagosome cargo recognition and loading, especially those effector proteins dependent on low abundance PI, such as PI5P and PI(3,5)P2.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential consequences of PI masking.

claim: In a recent report, a homozygous PIP4K2C mouse knockout displayed no growth or behavioral abnormalities.
source: In a recent report, a homozygous mouse knockout displayed no growth or behavioral abnormalities (Shim et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Shim et al., 2016.

claim: Starvation increases life spans across species.
source: Starvation increases life spans across species (Speakman and Hambly, 2007) and there are numerous diseases where upregulation of basal autophagy is beneficial (Hara et al., 2006; Seino et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Speakman and Hambly, 2007.

claim: There are numerous diseases where upregulation of basal autophagy is beneficial.
source: Starvation increases life spans across species (Speakman and Hambly, 2007) and there are numerous diseases where upregulation of basal autophagy is beneficial (Hara et al., 2006; Seino et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Hara et al., 2006; Seino et al., 2013.

claim: Mutant huntingtin itself may alter autophagy.
source: Mutant huntingtin itself may alter autophagy.
evidence: This is a statement about potential effects of mutant huntingtin.

claim: Wild-type huntingtin may be an adaptor for selected autophagic cargoes including itself.
source: Wild-type huntingtin may be an adaptor for selected autophagic cargoes including itself (Martinez-Vicente et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Martinez-Vicente et al., 2010.

claim: Mutant huntingtin impairs the loading of ubiquitinated-tagged proteins into autophagosomes.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, mutant huntingtin impairs the loading of ubiquitinated-tagged proteins into autophagosomes (Martinez-Vicente et al., 2010), and circumvents its own clearance (Martin et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Martinez-Vicente et al., 2010.

claim: Mutant huntingtin circumvents its own clearance.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, mutant huntingtin impairs the loading of ubiquitinated-tagged proteins into autophagosomes (Martinez-Vicente et al., 2010), and circumvents its own clearance (Martin et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Martin et al., 2015.

claim: Mutant huntingtin sequesters diverse proteins required for key cellular processes.
source: Moreover, mutant huntingtin sequesters diverse proteins required for key cellular processes (Kim et al., 2016), including mTOR, which plays key roles in the regulation of autophagy (Tsvetkov et al., 2013; Petersén A et al., 2001; Ravikumar et al., 2004; Pryor et al., 2014; Ashkenazi et al., 2017; Caviston et al., 2007; Wong and Holzbaur, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Kim et al., 2016; Tsvetkov et al., 2013; Petersén A et al., 2001; Ravikumar et al., 2004; Pryor et al., 2014; Ashkenazi et al., 2017; Caviston et al., 2007; Wong and Holzbaur, 2014.

claim: mTOR plays key roles in the regulation of autophagy.
source: Moreover, mutant huntingtin sequesters diverse proteins required for key cellular processes (Kim et al., 2016), including mTOR, which plays key roles in the regulation of autophagy (Tsvetkov et al., 2013; Petersén A et al., 2001; Ravikumar et al., 2004; Pryor et al., 2014; Ashkenazi et al., 2017; Caviston et al., 2007; Wong and Holzbaur, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Tsvetkov et al., 2013; Petersén A et al., 2001; Ravikumar et al., 2004; Pryor et al., 2014; Ashkenazi et al., 2017; Caviston et al., 2007; Wong and Holzbaur, 2014.

claim: The PI binding autophagy adaptor protein ALFY plays a fundamental role in degrading mutant huntingtin.
source: In addition, the PI binding autophagy adaptor protein ALFY which plays a fundamental role in degrading mutant huntingtin is down-regulated in HD (Martin et al., 2015; Filimonenko et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Martin et al., 2015; Filimonenko et al., 2010.

claim: ALFY is down-regulated in HD.
source: In addition, the PI binding autophagy adaptor protein ALFY which plays a fundamental role in degrading mutant huntingtin is down-regulated in HD (Martin et al., 2015; Filimonenko et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Martin et al., 2015; Filimonenko et al., 2010.

claim: There are studies that indicate that autophagy is not impaired in HD, and have revealed an elevation of autophagy flux in HD cells.
source: In contrast with these findings, there are studies that indicate that autophagy is not impaired in HD, and have revealed an elevation of autophagy flux in HD cells (Petersén A et al., 2001; Kegel et al., 2000).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Petersén A et al., 2001; Kegel et al., 2000.

claim: Upregulation of autophagy remains a viable approach for lowering levels of mutant huntingtin and aggregates.
source: Despite possible mutant huntingtin-dependent changes on autophagy, upregulation of autophagy remains a viable approach for lowering levels of mutant huntintin and aggregates (Lin and Qin, 2013; Sarkar et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lin and Qin, 2013; Sarkar et al., 2007.

claim: Caloric restriction raises the basal level of autophagy, leading to improvements in HD models.
source: Note that caloric restriction also raises the basal level of autophagy, leading to improvements in HD models (Duan et al., 2003) and increasing axonal autophagosome transport (Ikenaka et al., 2013), although it is less clear how to translate this observation into clinical practice.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Duan et al., 2003; Ikenaka et al., 2013.

claim: Caloric restriction increases axonal autophagosome transport.
source: Note that caloric restriction also raises the basal level of autophagy, leading to improvements in HD models (Duan et al., 2003) and increasing axonal autophagosome transport (Ikenaka et al., 2013), although it is less clear how to translate this observation into clinical practice.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Ikenaka et al., 2013.

claim: Rapamycin, an inhibitor of mTORC1, reduces mHtt protein levels.
source: Indeed, rapamycin, an inhibitor of mTORC1 also reduces mHtt protein levels (Sarkar et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sarkar et al., 2009.

claim: It is not yet clear whether PIP4Kγ inhibition results in mTORC1 inhibition or activation.
source: However, while PIP4Kγ likely impacts mTORC1 activity, it is not yet clear whether PIP4Kγ inhibition results in mTORC1 inhibition or activation.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: One study showed that knock-down of PIP4K2C inhibits mTORC1.
source: One study showed that knock-down of PIP4K2C inhibits mTORC1 (Mackey et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Mackey et al., 2014.

claim: In PIP4K2C homozygous knock-out mice, mTORC1 is elevated.
source: However, in PIP4K2C homozygous knock-out mice, mTORC1 is elevated (Shim et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Shim et al., 2016.

claim: Inhibition of mTOR via torin treatment exhibited a large increase in both autophagosome formation and autophagy flux.
source: While inhibition of mTOR via torin treatment exhibited a large increase in both autophagosome formation and autophagy flux, inhibition of PIP4Kγ had only a modest impact on autophagosome formation, but had a large increase in autophagic flux (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Inhibition of PIP4Kγ had only a modest impact on autophagosome formation, but had a large increase in autophagic flux.
source: While inhibition of mTOR via torin treatment exhibited a large increase in both autophagosome formation and autophagy flux, inhibition of PIP4Kγ had only a modest impact on autophagosome formation, but had a large increase in autophagic flux (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Elucidation of the mechanism whereby PIP4Kγ inhibition increases autophagic flux remains to be fully determined.
source: Thus, elucidation of the mechanism whereby PIP4Kγ inhibition increases autophagic flux remains to be fully determined.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: Inhibition of PIP4Kγ increases autophagic flux at least in part via the resulting impact on the levels of selected phosphoinositide lipids.
source: It is likely that inhibition of PIP4Kγ increases autophagic flux at least in part via the resulting impact on the levels of selected phosphoinositide lipids.
evidence: This is inferred from the changes in PI levels and their known roles in autophagy.

claim: Using NCT-504, no significant change in PI5P levels or other PI lipids was observed following up to two hours of inhibition of PIP4Kγ.
source: Using NCT-504 we found no significant change in PI5P levels or other PI lipids following up to two hours of inhibition of PIP4Kγ.
evidence: This statement is based on data from kinetic measurements of PI levels.

claim: Direct inhibition of PIKfyve results in an acute loss of PI(3,5)P2 which can be observed within 5 min.
source: This contrasts with other lipid kinases such as PIKfyve, where direct inhibition results in an acute loss of PI(3,5)P2 which can be observed within 5 min (Zolov et al., 2012; McCartney et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Zolov et al., 2012; McCartney et al., 2014.

claim: The long delay prior to changes in PI5P following PIP4Kγ inhibition suggests that PIP4Kγ is not in contact with most of the cellular PI5P, or is only active under specific conditions.
source: The long delay prior to changes in PI5P following PIP4Kγ inhibition suggests that PIP4Kγ is not in contact with most of the cellular PI5P, or is only active under specific conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the delayed changes in PI5P levels.

claim: After 12 hr treatment with NCT-504, there was a 1.6 fold elevation of PI5P.
source: However, after 12 hr treatment with NCT-504, there was a 1.6 fold elevation of PI5P.
evidence: This statement is based on data from PI measurements.

claim: At 12 hr, PI(3,5)P2 levels were elevated at 2-fold following NCT-504 treatment.
source: The fact that this change occurred well after 2 hr of inhibition, suggests that it might not be directly due to an accumulation of the PI5P substrate normally used by PIP4Kγ. Indeed, at 12 hr PI(3,5)P2 levels were also elevated at 2-fold, which was even higher than the fold elevation in PI5P.
evidence: This statement is based on data from PI measurements.

claim: The development of selective PIP4Kγ inhibitors could be extraordinarily useful for other neurodegenerative diseases.
source: From the translational point of view, the development of selective PIP4Kγ inhibitors could be extraordinarily useful for other neurodegenerative diseases as well.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications.

claim: Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease are mediated by the accumulation of toxic protein aggregates.
source: Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease in particular are also mediated by the accumulation of toxic protein aggregates, whose catabolism by autophagy might rescue stressed neurons.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about these diseases.

claim: Catabolism of toxic protein aggregates by autophagy might rescue stressed neurons in Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease.
source: Alzheimer's disease and Parkinson's disease in particular are also mediated by the accumulation of toxic protein aggregates, whose catabolism by autophagy might rescue stressed neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic approaches.

claim: There is only one type II PIP kinase homologue in Drosophila (dPIPK4 also called CG17471).
source: Unlike mammals, which have three PIP type II enzymes (PIP4Kalpha, PIP4Kbeta and PIP4Kγ), there is only one type II PIP kinase homologue in Drosophila (dPIPK4 also called CG17471) (Mackey et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Mackey et al., 2014.

claim: Reducing dPIP4K activity using different genetic approaches mitigates mHtt pathogenesis in three different assays in Drosophila.
source: Thus, reducing the activity of dPIP4K using different genetic approaches mitigates mHtt pathogenesis in three different assays.
evidence: This statement is based on data from Drosophila experiments.

claim: Inhibiting PIP4Kγ activity modulates productive autophagy, reduces mHtt protein levels in patient fibroblasts, and clears mHtt aggregates in neuronal cell models.
source: We show that inhibiting PIP4Kγ activity modulates productive autophagy, reduces mHtt protein levels in patient fibroblasts, and clears mHtt aggregates in neuronal cell models.
evidence: This statement is based on data from multiple experiments.

claim: Inhibition of PIP4Kγ rescues mHtt-induced neurodegeneration in two Drosophila HD models.
source: Moreover, we show that inhibition of PIP4Kγ rescues mHtt-induced neurodegeneration in two Drosophila HD models.
evidence: This statement is based on data from Drosophila experiments.

claim: Previous studies observed that knock-down of PIP4Kγ resulted in an increase in autophagy.
source: However, in line with our current findings, previous studies observed that knock-down of PIP4Kγ resulted in an increase in autophagy (Mackey et al., 2014; Vicinanza et al., 2015), and a reduction of EGFP-HttQ74 aggregates in MEFs that was dependent on the presence of the autophagy gene, ATG7 (Mackey et al., 2014; Vicinanza et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Mackey et al., 2014; Vicinanza et al., 2015.

claim: Previous studies observed a reduction of EGFP-HttQ74 aggregates in MEFs following knock-down of PIP4Kγ that was dependent on the presence of the autophagy gene, ATG7.
source: However, in line with our current findings, previous studies observed that knock-down of PIP4Kγ resulted in an increase in autophagy (Mackey et al., 2014; Vicinanza et al., 2015), and a reduction of EGFP-HttQ74 aggregates in MEFs that was dependent on the presence of the autophagy gene, ATG7 (Mackey et al., 2014; Vicinanza et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Mackey et al., 2014; Vicinanza et al., 2015.

claim: Inhibition of mTORC1 via torin treatment causes an increase in the induction of autophagy as well as an increase in autophagic flux.
source: In addition, as previously reported, torin treatment elevated both the number of autophagosomes and autolysosomes, because inhibition of mTORC1 causes an increase in the induction of autophagy as well as an increase in autophagic flux.
evidence: This statement is based on data from GFP-mCherry-LC3 reporter experiments and established knowledge about torin.

claim: Bafilomycin treatment results in an increase in autophagosomes because the subsequent formation of autolysosomes is blocked.
source: As previously reported, bafilomycin treatment resulted in an increase in autophagosomes because the subsequent formation of autolysosomes is blocked.
evidence: This statement is based on data from GFP-mCherry-LC3 reporter experiments and established knowledge about bafilomycin.

claim: mHtt-dependent effects seem to be triggered by aging.
source: It has not escaped our attention that mHtt-dependent effects seem to be triggered by aging, which is known to limit the clearance of misfolded proteins (Komatsu et al., 2007), and deregulate phosphatidylinositide lipid signaling (Igwe and Filla, 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Komatsu et al., 2007; Igwe and Filla, 1995.

claim: Aging is known to limit the clearance of misfolded proteins.
source: It has not escaped our attention that mHtt-dependent effects seem to be triggered by aging, which is known to limit the clearance of misfolded proteins (Komatsu et al., 2007), and deregulate phosphatidylinositide lipid signaling (Igwe and Filla, 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Komatsu et al., 2007.

claim: Aging is known to deregulate phosphatidylinositide lipid signaling.
source: It has not escaped our attention that mHtt-dependent effects seem to be triggered by aging, which is known to limit the clearance of misfolded proteins (Komatsu et al., 2007), and deregulate phosphatidylinositide lipid signaling (Igwe and Filla, 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Igwe and Filla, 1995.
